title: The emerging skillset of wielding coding agents — Beyang Liu, Sourcegraph / Amp
talk_summary: Beyang Liu describes how coding-agent power users get better results by giving agents richer context, reliable feedback loops, subagents, and parallel workstreams rather than micromanaging every edit. He also warns that agentic chains are tightly coupled to model/tool-use quality and that agents should be used to make reviews more thorough, not to skip understanding.

takeaways.what_they_do: They implement search as a subagent and recommend subagents for longer subtasks so the subtask’s context does not pollute the main agent’s context window.
Power users tell the agent exactly how to run builds/tests in unusual subdirectories, and use Playwright plus Storybook for fast front-end snapshot loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: tell it how to run, you know, the build in this particular subdirectory or run the tests

takeaways.what_they_do: They observed top users write long, detailed prompts because LLMs follow context and instructions; Amp even made Enter insert a newline to encourage this.
takeaways.evidence_quote: LMS are actually quite programmable. If you give them a lot of context, they will follow those instructions

takeaways.what_they_do: For large diffs, they ask the agent to summarize the diff and identify the best review entry point before doing a more thorough review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ask the agent to consume the diff and generate a high level summary

takeaways.what_they_do: Top users run multiple agents in parallel; one example constructs prompts for three or four agents on different parts of a compiler and lets them run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: constructs prompts for like three or four different agents to to work on different parts

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue agentic chains are deeply coupled to the model and that many models are not good at basic tool use, so swapping models is not equivalent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of the LMS out there aren't even good at the basics of tool use yet
